title: Fractional batching warmup scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
- Quick scratchpad to capture observations from running fractional-batching (early-dispatch of partial batches when idle threshold crossed) during warmup sequences and mixed ingress patterns.
- Trying to answer: can fractional batching reduce early-warmup tail latency without killing steady-state throughput or increasing token cost?

Experiment matrix (short):
- Model: hornet-7B-quant (FP16 fallback), seq_len=1024
- HW: p4d.24xlarge-like (8x A100 equivalent)
- Baseline: strict-full-batch dispatch (wait until batch size >= 32 or 10ms timer)
- Variant A: fractional-batch at 0.5 (dispatch when occupancy >= 50%)
- Variant B: fractional-batch at 0.25 with jittered timers
- Variant C: fractional-batch + KV-cache prefill for 10% LRU keys (warmup priming)
- Arrival patterns: steady Poisson (qps=120), diurnal ramp, microburst (1000rps for 300ms every 30s), mixed client blend (10% long-context, 90% short)
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (request completion), tokens/sec throughput, GPU utilization, tail-token-cost estimate (tokens-per-inference * cost weight)

Run notes (timestamps local):
- 2026-01-20 11:13: baseline vs A (Poisson steady):
  - Baseline p99: 167ms, p95: 82ms, throughput stable at 115 tokens/s, GPU util 72%
  - A (0.5): p99: 148ms (-11%), p95: 78ms (-5%), throughput 112 tokens/s (-2.6%), GPU util 69%
  - Immediate takeaway: fractional=0.5 trims p99 during low variance arrivals with small steady cost to throughput.

- 2026-01-20 13:05 microburst test (every 30s spike):
  - Baseline p99 (microburst windows): 420ms (heavy tail during spikes), many requests queued; recovery ~1.2s to baseline
  - A (0.5): p99: 470ms (worse), observed more context-switches on device and increased GPU kernel launch overhead; throughput spikes but more oscillation
  - B (0.25 + jitter): p99: 390ms (improved over baseline), jittered timers seem to smooth the kernel bursts; throughput 109 tokens/s
  - C (0.25 + KV prefill): p99: 280ms (huge improvement), warm cache reduced first-token overhead in spike windows
  - Note: fractional alone hurt microburst recovery unless paired with randomness or cache priming.

ASCII sketch of latency vs time (microburst window, normalized):
- baseline:  [__|_______^________|__]  (tail spike ~0.42s)
- A (0.5):       [__|________^^_______|_]
- B (0.25+j):     [__|______^__________|_]
- C (0.25+prefill):[__|__^____^_________|_]  (lower peak, faster decay)

Operational observations:
- Partial-batch dispatch reduces enqueue waiting time but increases number of kernel invocations per unit time; this matters for small models where kernel launch overhead is non-negligible.
- Burst sensitivity: when many partial batches hit simultaneously, kernel contention increases and KV cache misses amplify the effect. Without prefill, fractional can make tails worse during tight microbursts.
- Jitter on the batching timer (random 0-3ms) is surprisingly effective at de-synchronizing clients and reduces simultaneous kernel launches.
- Prefill policy: pre-populate KV caches for the top 10% of hot prompts (based on trace) reduces first-token penalty. A cheap heuristic: prime top-k keys once every 60s during idle windows.

Cost/throughput tradeoffs (rough):
- Baseline: cost unit = 1.0 (reference), throughput = 115 tokens/s
- A (0.5): cost unit = 1.02, throughput -2.6%
- B (0.25+j): cost = 1.05, throughput -4.5% but p99 improved in mixed flows
- C (0.25+prefill): cost = 1.08 (prefill token overhead), throughput -3.5%, p99 improved by ~33% in bursts

Quick hypotheses to validate next:
1) Adaptive fractional threshold: make fractional ratio a function of recent queue depth (e.g., lower fractional during detected microburst waves). Should reduce worst-case tails while preserving average gains.
2) Combine fractional batching with admission control: if instantaneous kernel queue depth > threshold, temporarily raise fractional cutoff to force larger batches (opposite direction).
3) Explore per-tenant warmup prefills tied to usage fingerprint; cheaper to prefill small hot-key sets than global priming.
4) Instrument kernel launch latency per-model variant: quantify launch cost vs per-token compute to set safe fractional ratios per-model.

Actionable next steps (short):
- Implement a simple adaptive-threshold knob in the local runtime binary (flag: --fractional-threshold-adaptive) and run the microburst replay harness (linked PR) (owner: Aisha).
- Add jitter to batching timer by default behind experimental flag; measure synchronization reduction across 5 runs. (owner: Ravi)
- Draft a short runbook entry for SRE: when enabling fractional, also enable KV-prefill for high-frequency tenants during launch/warm windows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How does fractional behave on large models (70B) where kernel launch amortization is higher? Expect less harm. Run one quick 70B check.
- How does warmup interplay with endpoint-level canary rollouts where two model versions have different fractional defaults? Risk of noisy splitting.
- Decide default for hosted: off for all until adaptive mode validated in 2-week A/B.

Notes-to-self:
- Save traces under: s3://redwood-experiments/fractional-warmup/2026-01-20/*
- Add small script to compute per-window kernel-call-rate (ccount) vs p99 to drive adaptive threshold policy.
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime "fractional warmup followups" (pinned messages)

End of scratchpad.

-- Thomas
